title: Drop Repeats From a Sorted Chain
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list whose values are sorted in non-decreasing order. Remove nodes so that every value appears exactly once, keeping one node for each value. Return the head of the resulting list, which is still sorted.

In tests a list is written as an array of its values, so [1, 1, 2] is the chain 1 → 1 → 2.

examples.why: Each run of equal values collapses to one node. The run of three 3s needs two removals in a row, not one.
An empty list has nothing to remove.
Keep exactly one 4. Values that repeat are kept once, not dropped completely.

constraints: The list is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: The list is sorted, so equal values are next to each other. Where is the copy of a value you need to compare against?
Stand on a node and look at its next node. If they hold the same value, the next one is a repeat.
Unlink the repeat with cur.next = cur.next.next and stay where you are. Only move forward when the next value is different.

explain.intuition:
Sorting puts every copy of a value in one run, so a repeat is always right after the node it repeats. Walk the list with one pointer cur and compare it with cur.next.

If the next node has the same value, skip over it by pointing cur.next one node further. Do not move cur yet, because the new next node might be another copy. Move only when the next value differs. The head never changes, because the first node is always the one kept for its value.
steps: While cur and cur.next exist: if cur.next.val === cur.val, set cur.next = cur.next.next.
pitfalls: Moving cur forward after every removal, which leaves the third copy in a run of three.
Dropping every value that repeats instead of keeping one copy. That is a different, harder problem.
Not handling an empty list: check cur before reading cur.next.

solutions.title: Rebuild with a dummy head
solutions.idea: Walk the input and append a node to a new chain only when its value differs from the last value appended.
solutions.space: O(1) extra besides the reused nodes

solutions.title: Unlink repeats in place
solutions.idea: Compare each node with its next; skip the next node while it repeats, otherwise move on.

followups: Remove every value that appears more than once, keeping only values that were unique to begin with.
The list is not sorted. How do you remove repeats, and what does it cost in time and memory?
